previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for a left total knee arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis. The surgery was performed successfully, and she tolerated the procedure well. Postoperatively, she developed mild anemia with a hematocrit drop to 25% on postoperative day 4, requiring a partial red blood cell transfusion of 1.25 units, after which her levels improved to 29.7%. Pain was managed initially with a PCA pump, then transitioned to oral medications including morphine and acetaminophen. She began physical therapy on postoperative day 1, was ambulating with a walker, and voiding independently after Foley removal on day 2. Her wound healed well with no signs of infection. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions on anticoagulation, wound care, activity, and follow-up. Her chronic conditions, including asthma, hypertension, and rheumatoid arthritis, were managed throughout the stay without complication.

patient however she is asymptomatic with rapid heart rates. Her

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with tachycardia, nausea, vomiting. 
Question acute process.

FINDINGS:  Portable frontal chest radiograph demonstrates stable findings of
right upper lobectomy, with increased tenting of the right hemidiaphragm which
may be the result of subsegmental atelectasis.  The left lung remains clear. 
The heart size is normal.  The mediastinal contours are notable for
calcifications in the right hilum and of the aortic arch.  A left chest
meta-port is stable in appearance with its tip within the left brachiocephalic
vein.  There is stable bilateral total shoulder arthroplasty.

IMPRESSION:  Post-surgical changes right upper lobectomy, with increased
volume loss on the right compared with ___.

CT OF THE CHEST WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST, CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST, CT
OF THE PELVIS WITH CONTRAST, ___, AT 1403 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Tachycardia with history of cancer.  Elevated liver enzymes.

TECHNIQUE:  Serial transverse images were acquired sequentially through the
chest before and after the uneventful administration of 130 mL of Omnipaque
350.  Imaging through the chest was performed per chest pain protocol with
optimized opacification of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.  Initial portal
venous phase delay was then administered and scanning was performed through
the abdomen and pelvis per clinical concern.  Multiplanar reformatted images
were generated both of the chest and abdominopelvic data sets.

FINDINGS:

CHEST:  Again noted is post-surgical evidence of a prior right upper
lobectomy.  Fibrotic changes in the anterior right hemithorax are presumed due
to prior radiation therapy, correlate clinically.  There is a linear
dystrophic calcification and ill-defined scarring noted centrally within the
right breast.  This is stable relative to prior exams.  

No focal consolidation or superimposed edema is noted.  There is no pleural
effusion or pneumothorax. No suspicious pulmonary nodules or masses seen. 
Unlike the prior exam, there is no irregularity noted along the right lateral
margin of the trachea.  The airway, while suboptimally evaluated in
end-expiratory phase, is widely patent with no endoluminal lesions identified.


There is no pulmonary embolism.  The main pulmonary artery is normal in size. 
The thoracic aorta is normal in contour, caliber, and course.  Normal
three-vessel origin of the great vessels is identified.  No pneumomediastinum
is identified.  There are 11 mm and 12 mm short axis lymph nodes in the right
paratracheal distribution, indicating underlying adenopathy.  The overall
involved lymph nodes are relatively small in number.  There is diffuse
circumferential wall thickening of the esophagus throughout its course in the
mediastinum, of indeterminate etiology.  The heart is enlarged.  There is
coronary artery plaque.  No pericardial effusion is evident.

ABDOMEN/PELVIS:  The solid abdominal organs of the upper abdomen are
unremarkable.  No intrahepatic biliary dilatation is noted.  Both kidneys
enhance symmetrically with no hydronephrosis.  The gallbladder is present but
incompletely distended with no wall thickening, gallstones, or pericholecystic
inflammation.

The stomach is collapsed, as are the imaged small bowel loops.  No dilatation
or wall thickening evident.  A normal appendix is identified.  The bowel is
largely collapsed.  High attenuation mixed with stool is noted distally. 
There are extensive left-sided diverticula.  In particular, there is a
relatively large rectosigmoid diverticulum noted deep in the pelvis.  No
diverticulitis is evident.

Scattered calcified plaque is seen and otherwise unremarkable aortoiliac
vasculature.  No pathologic lymphadenopathy is seen within the abdomen or
pelvis.  There is no free intraperitoneal fluid or air noted.  The uterus and
ovaries are age appropriate and are unremarkable.  The bladder is distended
with no wall thickening or internal filling defects noted.  There are ovoid
fluid-attenuation foci surrounding the urethra at the base of the bladder. 
These are of indeterminate etiology, but were present on the prior exam. 
Urethral diverticula are suspected.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is a subacute vs. chronic ununited lateral right
seventh rib fracture.  Otherwise, no suspicious osseous lesions or other
fractures identified.  Chronic grade 2 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 with
extensive L4-L5 disc degeneration is again noted and remains stable compared
to prior exams.  The remaining spine is normally aligned.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No PE or acute aortic syndrome.
2.  Diffuse full-length circumferential esophageal wall thickening, likely
indicating esophagitis; however, of unknown etiology.
3.  Tracheal abnormality previously noted is no longer present.  The lumen is
patent with no endoluminal lesions noted.
4.  Dystrophic calcification in the right breast and fibrotic changes in the
anterior right lung are stable and presumed related to prior radiation.
5.  Coronary artery disease and cardiomegaly.
6.  Ovoid fluid collections around the urethra at the base of the bladder. 
These are stable since at least ___ and may represent small urethral
diverticulae.  Correlate clinically.
7.  Subacute vs. chronic ununited lateral right seventh rib fracture.

osseous malignant process with old rib fractures on the right.
